items.prompt:
What digital tool would MOST help a student check spelling while typing a report?
A) A dictionary book
B) Spell-check software
C) A ruler
D) A pencil

steps: Spell-check is a digital tool built into word processors that automatically flags misspelled words.

items.prompt:
Which of the following is an example of PUBLISHING writing with digital tools?
A) Erasing a mistake
B) Drawing a picture
C) Posting a story on the class website for others to read
D) Writing in a paper journal

steps: Publishing means sharing writing with an audience. Posting on a class website is a digital form of publishing.

items.prompt: True or False: When you type a story on a computer, it is easy to delete a word and replace it with a better one.

steps: Word processors allow easy editing — you can delete and retype without making the page messy.

items.prompt:
A student and her partner want to write a report together. They are at home on different computers. Which digital tool would BEST let them both work on the same document at the same time?
A) A printer
B) Spell-check
C) A shared online document (like Google Docs)
D) A calculator

steps: A shared online document allows two or more users to write and edit the same file simultaneously from different locations.

items.prompt:
Spell-check does NOT catch every mistake. Which of the following errors would spell-check MISS?
A) Typing 'frend' instead of 'friend'
B) Typing 'their' when you mean 'there'
C) Typing 'recieve' instead of 'receive'
D) Typing 'becuase' instead of 'because'

steps: Spell-check only flags words that are not in the dictionary. 'Their' is a correctly spelled word, so spell-check will not flag it even if 'there' was the intended word.

items.prompt: How is posting a story on a SCHOOL WEBSITE different from printing it and hanging it on a CLASSROOM BULLETIN BOARD? Think about the audience.
items.answer: Posting on a school website makes the story available to anyone with internet access — parents, students at other schools, and people around the world. A bulletin board can only be seen by people who physically enter the classroom. The school website reaches a much larger audience.

steps: Website audience: global, anyone with internet.
Bulletin board audience: classroom visitors only.

items.prompt: A student finishes her digital story and is ready to publish. She wants to reach THREE different audiences: her classmates, her parents, and her grandparents who live far away. Describe a different publishing method for each audience and explain why each method is the best choice.
items.answer: Classmates: Post on the class website or shared class folder — classmates can access it on school devices. Parents: Email a copy or share a link to the school site — parents check their email regularly and can read it at home. Grandparents who live far away: Email it or share it through a video call where the student reads it aloud — emailing reaches them instantly regardless of distance.

steps: Match the publishing method to how each audience accesses information.
Distant relatives: email or video call.

items.prompt: Describe how a student could use digital tools at EVERY stage of writing a class report: planning, drafting, revising, and publishing. Name a specific tool for each stage.
items.answer: Planning: Use a digital graphic organizer or blank doc to outline ideas and organize them before drafting. Drafting: Type the first draft in a word processor (Google Docs, Microsoft Word), focusing on ideas without worrying about perfection. Revising: Re-read the draft; use copy/paste to move sentences, add details, and delete off-topic sections. Use spell-check to catch spelling errors. Publishing: Post the final formatted report on the class website, email it to parents, or print it for a class book.
